_comment: UPSTREAM TOOL INVENTORY for the AWS Kiro CLI (Amazon Q Developer CLI heritage). This file is a DRIFT TRIPWIRE, not configuration: tests/test_tool_inventory.py asserts every name here classifies to the stated class under the gate's VOCAB, and that none of them classify as 'unknown'. When upstream adds a tool, add it here with an explicit class; until then the gate treats it as UNKNOWN and gates it hardest, so the failure mode is over-block rather than a silent exfil channel (CBP review, thread harness-lane-split, 2026-07-24).
_provenance: DOCUMENTED-tier throughout. Kiro is a closed AWS product; these names come from Kiro/Amazon-Q documentation, NOT from source and NOT from a live install. Live confirmation belongs on an onboarding rig with an installed kiro CLI. Because the gate is fail-closed, a wrong name here over-blocks rather than admitting a call.
_classes: read = local read, may skip Gate-2 | write = mutates local files | exec = runs a command | egress = touches the network or a cloud API | mcp = MCP-family, argument shape is the server's

tools.name: fs_read
tools.note: Amazon Q's reader; tool_input key is `path`

tools.name: read
tools.note: Claude-lineage superset - Kiro's Claude heritage may surface it

tools.name: fs_write
tools.note: Amazon Q's writer; tool_input key is `path`

tools.name: execute_bash
tools.note: Amazon Q's shell; NOT Claude's Bash - an untranslated handoff gives the governor target=None

tools.name: use_aws
tools.note: An AWS API call: cloud read OR write OR exfil. Its parameter set is NOT fully documented - `profile_name` was missing from the original key whitelist (CBP KIRO-4), which is why every string leaf is now swept instead of a guessed key list.

_event_field: Kiro's stdin event-name field is DOCUMENTED as `hook_event_name` and is UNVERIFIED. Crush is the existence proof that this varies between engines. gate_core.should_gate() accepts `hook_event_name` or `event`, and gates any envelope carrying a tool_name even when neither is present, because exiting 0 on an unrecognized envelope disarms the gate on every call (CBP KIRO-3).
